summary: Sound and well-attributed: each judge shape is its own CUDA graph, so four layer-disjoint, shape-gated Triton paths should add up per load. Re-deriving from the five result.json files gives about +2.3% geomean over master (decode_1 ~6%, verify_1 ~5%, decode_16 ~3%, other loads flat), which is above the ~1.5% CI. No companion is needed because the per-shape rows already attribute each component. Dispatch it after the two in-flight pooler runs harvest, so pooler slot (1) uses the better variant and no check is spent twice.
justification: Mechanism: at m<=16 these are pure weight streams (pooler 67 MB, qkv_gate 37.7 MB, o 16.8 MB, unpooler slice 8.4 MB). cuBLAS runs nvjet plus a separate splitKreduce, which adds one kernel and one graph node (LESSONS: ~2-4 us per nvjet+reduce pair). The ticket-semaphore last-CTA reduce removes that node, and the full-K o kernel keeps 128 CTAs with 128-160 KB in flight. Both are plausible on H200, and the component runs confirm it. I re-checked them against master's check run (240eb/bd9f era, 1.151x). Paired ratios vs SGLang: pooler 1.071/1.068/1.059 at decode_1/verify_1/decode_16, against master 1.006/1.011/1.009 and ~0.99-1.00 in the other runs, so +5-7% on 20-21 us = 1.1-1.4 us per shape; this is the largest absolute lever and still 6 us above the 14 us floor. Unpooler slice 1.169/1.148 vs ~0.99-1.01, so ~1 us on a 7 us shape (floor 1.7). o 1.085/1.069 at decode_1/decode_16 vs ~1.00-1.01, ~0.4-0.5 us; verify_1 1.028 vs 1.020 is flat, as the hypothesis says. qkv_gate 1.029/1.044/1.024 vs a cross-run norm of ~1.00-1.01 (master's own 0.981 at decode_1 was a low draw, so the stated 14.4->13.8 overstates it), worth 0.2-0.45 us. Load sums with weights all 62: decode_1 ~55 -> ~52 us (~6%), verify_1 ~54 -> ~51.5 (~5%), decode_16 ~66 -> ~64 (~3%), decode_32/verify_16/verify_32 unchanged. Geomean ~exp((.058+.049+.030)/6) ~ 1.023, so ~1.17-1.18 for the run, against BEST 1.143 [1.126,1.160]. The expected shapes and directions in the frontmatter match this. Excluding m=32 is right: qkv 0.858, o 0.907 and pooler 0.994 there. Excluding unpooler n=8192 is right: 1.002-1.009 at m=16. Weakest link: the ~2.3% predicted gain rests on summing several 1-7% per-shape deltas, each measured in a different run against a single master run. The qkv_gate and o-verify_1 parts (2-4%) sit inside the 1.5-2.5% per-shape drift. Also, router verify_1 read 4.26-4.44x in all three dba4ffd-based component runs vs 4.61x on master (5.9-6.2 vs 5.7 us). verify_1 is the load most sensitive to the router (SGLang's router there is 26 us), so if that drop is systematic rather than drift it would take ~0.3-0.5 us off verify_1's ~2.8 us gain. The combined geomean should still clear the CI.
confounders: router-triton-hilo-fused-control-splitk-all-m: no confound. Router shapes are separate graphs and the router path is untouched. Its only coupling is the shared prepare() and caching-allocator state, which could explain the repeated router verify_1 dip in the component runs; that dip is drift-sized and on a shape this change does not route.

sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity: not a confounder but the incumbent. Every non-gated shape keeps _bf16_gemm_dispatch_impl, so a loss on a gated shape means Triton lost to nvjet. The gating rule was chosen from the same rows, so a mild winner's-curse regression toward ~1.0 is expected on the 2-4% components (qkv_gate, o verify_1).
router-hilo-at-m8: superseded wholesale by the split-K router on master. It has no effect on any bf16-layer shape.
interference: No companion is warranted. Each judge shape is timed as its own CUDA graph with a cold L2, and the four routed paths touch disjoint (layer, m) shapes. The per-shape rows of this single run therefore attribute each component directly. A gain on pooler rows is the pooler kernel; a qkv_gate row reading <=1.0 says drop qkv_gate. Neither a gain nor a loss is ambiguous at the component level. The ab-revert the author floats (drop qkv_gate) would only replay rows this run already reports, would cost one of bf16's 4 remaining checks, and cannot resolve a 2-4% effect better than the paired rows do. The landed hypotheses act on other shapes (router) or are the incumbent dispatch, so reverting or retuning them tells nothing about these kernels. Timing: do not dispatch while pooler-splitk2-tma-weight-stream and pooler-triton-splitk2-blockn64-semaphore-control-blockk256 are in the judge; wait one harvest. Pooler is the largest component (~1.2-1.4 us per shape), so choosing its variant decides most of the headline, and re-running the combo for a better pooler later would cost a second check. Choose the variant by its m<=16 pooler rows (paired ratio and top_kernels time), not by 'harvested as a gain'. A single-layer pooler change will almost certainly classify neutral vs BEST even if its kernel is faster, so the spec's trigger as written will never fire. The router split-K32 runs in flight need no wait: router is untouched here and their result composes independently.
rules_flags: None blocking. Routing is on cfg layer/m/n and tensor shapes only, never data. Weights stay BF16. ws/cnt buffers are allocated in prepare() and hold no input-derived state across calls: ws is overwritten each call, and cnt self-resets via atomic_xchg and is zeroed after warm-up. The same pattern passed the 9 tests plus timed-call checks in the pooler, qkv and unpooler runs. No host syncs. Allocation is only torch.empty for the output inside the graph, as the incumbent does.

Caveat on 'byte-for-byte the measured one': with POOLER_MAX_M and QKV_MAX_M lowered to 16, the WS_M constexpr changes from 32 to 16, so the ws offset math and the compiled specialization differ slightly from the measured kernels. This is harmless but should be noted in the attempt file. The ws shapes must stay [SPLIT_K, WS_M, N] with WS_M equal to the constant passed to the kernel.

Name collisions: the pooler and unpooler patches both define _bf16_splitk_kernel (and qkv's is _qkv_splitk_sem_kernel). Use one kernel body. Copy _pooler_skinny_kernel from pooler-triton-skinny-m32.patch, because master does not have it and the o patch assumes it. Keep a separate cnt per layer, because sharing one ticket array across layers inside a graph would be a correctness bug.

Compile budget: warm m in 1..16 for three layers plus 1..8 for the unpooler. Because of do_not_specialize=['M'] this is few compiles, but the warm-up must use exactly the BLOCK_M/constexpr combinations the timed call uses, so nothing compiles under graph capture. Keep the whole run well inside the 10-minute limit.
open_questions: Is the router verify_1 dip in all three dba4ffd-based component runs (4.26-4.44x vs master 4.61x) drift or systematic? If this run shows it again on an untouched shape, compare against the BEST submit run's per-shape router row before attributing any verify_1 change.
If both in-flight pooler variants harvest, pick the one with the lower m<=16 pooler kernel time. If TMA wins only at m=32, which is excluded here, keep the split-K2 BLOCK_K=128 baseline.

Should the qkv_gate slot go in at all? A component expected at ~+0.3 us per shape adds a third semaphore kernel and more compile time for under 0.2% geomean. Keeping it is defensible because the per-shape rows will settle it, but a follow-up should drop it if any of its three rows reads below ~1.01.
